attributes.body:
The は particle has two primary functions. The first is to mark the topic of a sentence, as learned very early in our Japanese language journey. However, the second common usage of は is to highlight contrast (making a comparison). When は is used after a number/counter, it regularly has this comparison meaning. This can be translated as 'or so', or 'at least'.

Before は, the counter is regularly followed by くらい (or ぐらい). This just softens the statement, and further highlights the 'or so' meaning.

Despite being translated as 'at least', the comparative meaning of は itself is what creates the nuance of this grammar structure. The thing before は is being highlighted as an amount, while also implying that there are other amounts. This implication of another amount makes は sound as if it could mean 'as opposed to (B)'. So in essence, this grammar structure sounds like 'As for (A), as opposed to (B)', where (B) is not usually mentioned.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: Both forms emphasize quantity, but with contrasting nuance. Number/Amount + は implies 'at least' that amount, with a contrastive tone. For example, ３０分はかかると思うけど ('I think it'll take at least 30 minutes.', implying that it won't be less, but might be more.). In contrast, Number + も emphasizes the amount as if the speaker believes it is a lot, e.g., ３０分もかかった ('It took thirty whole minutes.').

first_relatable.title: Number/Amount + は
first_relatable.meaning: At least, Sort of, Or so

attributes.body: These patterns are similar in that both combine a counting expression with a particle. Number/Amount + は has a contrastive nuance, implying 'at least' that amount. For example, １０人は来ると思うけど ('I think at least 10 people will come.', implying the speaker is uncertain if any more will.). In contrast, なん + counter + か means 'a few (A)' or 'several (A)', e.g. 何人か 'a few people.'

first_relatable.title: Number/Amount + は
first_relatable.meaning: At least, Sort of, Or so

attributes.body: When は follows a number or amount, it often adds a contrastive nuance like 'at least' or 'no more than.' For example, １回は行ったけど means 'I went once, but no more than that.' This is similar to contrastive uses of は, like in 田中さんは行ったけど ('Tanaka went, but no one else did'). If there's no contrast, the number is usually used without a particle, as in 三つ買った ('I bought three').
